name: rheon-which
description: What a name runs -- which, with every match on PATH and who put it there.
author: takakix2
notes:
By default it is which: the first match on PATH for each NAME, one line per path (exit 1 when a NAME is not found, said on stderr); -a lists every match in PATH order, as GNU which -a does (a PATH entry repeated, or /bin that links to /usr/bin, gives the same file twice). With --rheon: a command:found record for every match -- name, path, rank, wins (the one that runs), dir, ext (the extension Windows matched), link_target, same_file_as (the rank of an earlier match that is the same file) and placed_by -- then a terminator; a NAME with no match is a command:missing record, and the exit is 0.

placed_by is the rheon tool that put the match on the shelf (~/.local/bin), by the same rule rheon install uses (an installed declaration holds the name, and a short name is still a copy of the tool); anything put there by hand or by another package manager is null. Unix: each PATH directory in order, a file with an execute bit, an empty entry is the current directory (POSIX). Windows: each PATH directory in order (; separated, quotes removed), the name as typed if it has an extension and then with each PATHEXT extension; the current directory is not looked at first (as PowerShell and CreateProcess; cmd does). A NAME with a path separator is checked as that path. Aliases, functions and builtins of the calling shell are not visible from another program -- ask the shell (type, command -v). The library entry (run_in) takes PATH, PATHEXT, the home and the platform rule as arguments and never exits the process. Linux, macOS and Windows.
